<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard VCS package that clones a Git repository from the project's official GitHub URL. The `source` array uses `git+https`, which is a normal and expected method for AUR packages tracking development branches. The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` entry is appropriate for VCS sources and does not pose a risk during the `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` phase, as the command only fetches and extracts sources without executing any build or prepare functions.

The `pkgver()` function executes Git commands locally on the checked-out repository to generate a revision-based version string. It does not perform any network operations, execute downloaded code, or exfiltrate data. All operations in `pkgver()` are confined to the local Git repository state, which will be fetched from the declared upstream. There are no command substitutions, evals, or remote code executions in the global scope or `pkgver()`.

The `package()` function is irrelevant for this safety gate because it is not executed under `--noprepare --nobuild`. Therefore, no potentially dangerous operations (if any) inside it can run during this phase. Overall, sourcing this PKGBUILD and fetching its sources poses no immediate security risk.
</details>

This is a common and accepted practice, not a security flaw. There are no network operations, script executions, or file modifications defined in this file—only declarative metadata. The file does not execute code or download from untrusted sources.

No evidence of obfuscation, malicious payloads, or unauthorized system access is present. The package conflicts with and provides `waydroid-script`, indicating it is an alternative implementation, which is normal packaging behavior.
</details>
